_comment: Canonical current catalog for every governed dataset, model and reference asset. It is the only live source for identity, lifecycle, acquisition status, access limits, revisions and local verification. The original June/July frozen baseline remains embedded as the frozen-baseline profile; non-baseline and planned assets are in asset_catalog. Large bytes live under SPEECHRL_DATA_DIR and are never committed.
generated: 2026-08-15; acquisition wave 2 for the speech-aware study: SLURP, SLUE-SQA-5 and Spoken-SQuAD re-verified in place against their recommended variants, and HALAS, SlideASR-Bench and the SQuAD v1.1 dev reconstruction reference registered and closed by official-source verification

profiles.frozen-baseline: The reproducible June/July baseline; default fetch profile for backward compatibility.
profiles.local-candidates: Observed non-baseline local assets; presence does not authorize an experiment.
profiles.speech-aware-core: Earnings21, Earnings22 and ConEC Stage-2A minimum speech-domain closure.
profiles.speech-aware-diagnostics: PRISM, Rare5k and BuzzWord speech/entity diagnostic carriers.
profiles.speech-aware-secondary: SLUE-SQA-5, ContextASR-Bench, AMI and SlideASR-Bench public secondary speech carriers.
profiles.speech-aware-annotations: Annotation-only overlays that carry no speech bytes of their own: TED-EL (TED-LIUM3 audio remains source-unstable), HALAS over Earnings22, and the SQuAD v1.1 dev reference used to reconstruct the pre-deletion Spoken-SQuAD question list.
profiles.speech-aware-small-public: Small optional speech assets: ATCO2-1h, Eka-Medical and LibriSQA.
profiles.retained-cross-domain: Locally complete general/environmental-audio assets retained for reuse but excluded from the speech-aware study.
profiles.meeting-minutes-text: Text-layer meeting assets for the meeting-minutes-agent topic: MeetingQA and QMSum over AMI/ICSI transcripts, and the M3-SLU speaker-attributed text layer. None of these records carry speech bytes of their own.
profiles.meeting-minutes-speech: Speech-bearing meeting carriers for the meeting-minutes-agent topic: the ICSI Meeting Corpus mixed-headset signals and their CC BY annotation layers. Distinct from meeting-minutes-text, which carries no audio.
profiles.deferred: Cataloged but intentionally not in the current acquisition wave.

status_model.COMPLETE: Required bytes for this record are present at the recorded identity.
status_model.PARTIAL: Some bytes or metadata are present but the record is not complete.
status_model.MISSING: No governed local copy is present.
status_model.BLOCKED: Acquisition is prevented by access, source stability, publication or privacy constraints.

acquisition_policy.rule: Datasets larger than 1 TB are excluded from acquisition and from the active research reference set; retain only a tombstone catalog record so they cannot silently re-enter scope.

amendments.task: speech-aware acquisition wave 4 (SAEA half of the survey-confirmed shortlist): verify-then-fetch of SpokenNativQA and a scoped AudioBench speech bundle. Zero cost; no paid, gated or form-walled source was used. The meeting-domain half of the shortlist is deliberately NOT acquired here, pending an owner decision.

changes.note: SpokenNativQA registered as a spoken-QA secondary carrier. Verified before fetching: ungated, public, licence cc-by-nc-sa-4.0 declared on the card, and the official file list totals 364,209,997 bytes over 3,323 files, matching the survey's ~364 MB estimate exactly. Landed complete with byte closure: 3,323/3,323 files, 0 missing, 0 size mismatches, and all 3,311 LFS-backed files verified by SHA-256. The share-alike term is recorded as a claim limit because it attaches to redistributed derivatives. Acquisition note for future waves: the hf-mirror.com mirror does not serve this repository at all (repeated 'Local entry not found' against the pinned revision), so the official endpoint plus the aria2c-based hfd downloader is the working channel.

A scoped AudioBench speech bundle registered as one record with four member configs (common_voice_15_en_test, dream_tts_mcq_test, openhermes_instruction_test, alpaca_audio_test), 22 files and 3,524,177,488 bytes, every config landing with byte closure and zero LFS SHA-256 failures. The important finding is legal, not technical: the AudioLLMs repackagings declare NO licence of their own in either cardData or README, carrying only citations, so upstream terms govern and were made the selection criterion. Configs whose upstream terms are clear were taken; cn_college_listen_mcq_test and public_sg_speech_qa_test are HELD pending an owner licence ruling (exam-recording provenance and IMDA's separate terms respectively), and TED-LIUM 3 configs are held because its no-derivatives term conflicts with derived feature extraction. Sound/music and AudioSet- or FreeSound-derived configs were hard-excluded by the research boundary, paralinguistic configs excluded as outside 'speech and its linguistic content', and configs already governed at original-source identity excluded as duplicates. The full disposition is on the entry's scope_note.

Recording, not yet registering, three larger SAEA-half carriers whose transfers were still streaming when this amendment was written; each gets its own entry once byte closure is verified. SD-QA: official source is github.com/ffaisal93/SD-QA under Apache-2.0 (the WillHeld/SD-QA Hugging Face mirror declares no licence and was therefore not used); the English subset is 11 dialects (aus, gbr, ind_n, ind_s, irl, kenya, nga, nzl, phl, usa, zaf) across dev and test, with constant questions per dialect. Both git paths failed here — a blob-filtered partial clone stalled with a dead fetch, and the ghfast.top proxy returned HTTP 504 on the 6.4 GB pack — so the working channel is per-file raw.githubusercontent fetches at a pinned commit, driven by the audio_file column of each dialect metadata.csv (22,037 English wav). SpokenWOZ: licence CC BY-NC 4.0 per the official spokenwoz.github.io project page, which designates four Hugging Face repositories as the distribution point; those repositories themselves declare no licence, so the project page is the licence of record. Total 12,823,386,187 bytes over 4 repositories, free and ungated, no form. WearVox: ungated, public, cc-by-nc-4.0, 59,449,535,253 bytes over 7,688 files. Its payload splits into wav/ (3,842 mono files, 4.500 GB) and wav_mc/ (3,842 multichannel files, 54.894 GB) over the same recordings, so the mono half is fetched first as the part a mono-consuming frozen core can actually use. Measured official-endpoint throughput on large files is 3.16 MB/s, projecting roughly 5.2 hours for the full repository; the mirror serves nothing for this repository.

amendments.task: speech-aware acquisition wave 3: the SLURP label side is brought under governed local identity, and the AMI annotation archives plus the ContextASR-Dialogue English shards are materialised. No new bytes were fetched from any paid source; total program spend for this wave is zero.

changes.note: SLURP previously had 141,652 FLAC recordings on disk under datasets/slurp with no label side at that path -- the annotations existed only inside the reference checkout at repos/slurp/dataset. A governed copy of the seven label-side files (train/devel/test/train_synthetic.jsonl, metadata.json, lm.txt, LICENSE.txt) now lives at datasets/slurp/metadata with per-file SHA-256. Identity was proved rather than assumed: the git blob SHA-1 of every file was compared against the GitHub contents API at the pinned commit 8eb16545762be97ace75334109d73824217311f1 and all matched, and the checkout's working tree is diff-clean against that commit, so no re-download was warranted. The full audio reconcile now covers all four splits, not just the real ones: 141,648 unique recordings[] references resolve against the local inventory with 0 missing (100.00%), comprising 50,627 train + 8,690 devel + 13,078 test against 72,395 real FLAC and 69,253 against 69,257 synthetic FLAC. The 4 unreferenced files are all synthetic and form one contiguous generation-timestamp cluster; the real side stays exactly one-for-one, reproducing the 2026-08-15 finding. License is split and is now recorded verbatim on the entry: the textual part is CC BY 4.0 and the audio part is CC BY-NC 4.0, which constrains audio-derived results to non-commercial research use.

The two AMI annotation archives were extracted in place into version-named subdirectories (manual_1.6.2/ and auto_1.5.1/). Entry counts reproduce the 2026-08-04 CRC audit exactly (5,183 and 4,312) and both archives re-tested CRC PASS; the zips are unmodified. Extraction yielded 5,158 files / 205,293,665 bytes and 4,295 files / 809,561,283 bytes respectively, the shortfall against entry counts being directory records. This is what makes the meeting-domain label layers reachable: the manual set carries namedEntities, topics, dialogueActs, segments, words and both abstractive and extractive summaries. Receipt at datasets/ami/annotations/extraction-receipt.json. No unzip binary exists on this host and installing one is prohibited, so extraction used the Python standard-library zipfile module.

ContextASR-Dialogue English was extracted from its 6 resident tar shards (25,562,296,320 archive bytes) into datasets/contextasr-bench/audio/ContextASR-Dialogue/English, matching the relative audio paths in the shipped index. Every shard carries a SHA-256 computed in a single pass during extraction; shards 1 and 2 were additionally re-read and reproduced identical digests. The subset closes completely against its index: 5,273 of 5,273 records resolve, 0 missing, 0 WAV header failures, 0 decode failures on a seeded 25-file sample, and 0 duration mismatches over 0.5s, with measured duration equal to declared duration at 798,687.24 seconds (221.858 hours) across 25,558,223,694 extracted bytes. Media shape: 70,038 dialogue turns over 3 to 5 distinct speakers, 58,741 entity mentions and 3,733 distinct movie_name values. Following the sibling ContextASR-Speech English receipt, the reference transcript text and the per-dialogue entity_list were counted but deliberately not materialised, pending the owner ruling on their legal/ceiling tier. Receipt at derived/carrier-manifests/2026-08-17/contextasr-dialogue-english.manifest.json. Process note for auditors: the first extraction pass covered only shards 1-5 because the shard list was read from a truncated directory listing rather than a glob; the index reconcile caught the resulting 273-file tail gap (ids 12499-13209) and shard 6 was then extracted, after which the subset closed exactly. The Mandarin subsets remain unextracted and are out of scope for this English-only study.

Recording, not changing, a SLURP storage redundancy found during this wave. The same audio payload is reachable at both datasets/slurp and repos/slurp/scripts/audio as distinct files rather than links, and both source archives (slurp_real.tar.gz 3,918,185,662 bytes and slurp_synth.tar.gz 2,839,670,545 bytes) are retained alongside their extracted contents. Measured apparent size is 26G under datasets/slurp and 13G under repos/slurp. Note that DrvFS synthesises inode numbers, so the link-versus-copy determination rests on the du figures rather than on inode identity. Nothing was deleted: reclaiming this space is an owner decision, and the entry's local_subdir still points at repos/slurp/scripts/audio.

amendments.task: speech-aware acquisition wave 2: three on-disk re-verifications and three new registrations

changes.note: Re-verified three existing holdings against their recommended variants; no bytes were re-downloaded and no identity, revision or size field was changed. SLURP: the governed holding is the ORIGINAL upstream variant (pinned pswietojanski/slurp checkout plus the Zenodo 4274930 audio release), a superset of the qmeeus/slurp HF repackaging; 72,395 real FLAC recordings on disk reconcile one-for-one with the 72,395 unique recordings referenced by train/devel/test.jsonl (0 missing, 0 unreferenced), 69,257 synthetic recordings are also present, and the four official jsonl indexes carry per-utterance entities/slot spans plus per-recording wer and ent_wer. SLUE-SQA-5: sqa5 holds verified_test (3 shards, 408 rows), test (14 shards, 2,382 rows), validation (12 shards, 1,939 rows) and train (270 shards, 46,186 rows), each with document_audio and raw_document_text columns; the two requested evaluation splits were already resident, so the do-not-fetch instruction for train had no acquisition effect and no local data was deleted. Spoken-SQuAD: the AudioLLMs/spoken_squad_test mirror is byte-complete at the pinned revision (23 payload files, 3,403,613,158 bytes, 5,351 rows).

Explaining, not changing, the spoken-squad legacy fingerprint. The recorded files=25 / size_bytes=3403615926 counts two non-payload downloader bookkeeping files under .hfd (last_download_command 162 bytes and repo_metadata.json 2,606 bytes; 2,768 bytes total) on top of the 23 governed payload files totalling 3,403,613,158 bytes, which match the pinned upstream file list exactly. The record is left as-is so the historical fingerprint stays reproducible.

Registered three new assets. HALAS: span-level ASR hallucination annotations over Earnings-22, no audio of its own. SlideASR-Bench: entity-dense contextual-ASR secondary carrier pinned as a whole repository because upstream serves one audio tree for both split indexes; consumption is scoped to the test split audio plus per-example entity_list, with slide images and train.jsonl explicitly unused. SQuAD v1.1 dev: text-only reconstruction reference for the pre-deletion Spoken-SQuAD question list, needed because the AudioLLMs mirror ships only the 5,335 surviving question texts, exposes no question_id, and omits 5,198 of the 10,570 original dev questions.

HALAS is recorded with its upstream license field verbatim as "unknown"; no SPDX identifier, LICENSE file or terms text is published upstream. The entry carries license_note UNRESOLVED_FOR_PUBLICATION and a claim_limit blocking redistribution, derived release and any Stage-3 publication use until the terms are resolved in writing.

Extended two profile descriptions to cover the new members: speech-aware-secondary now names SlideASR-Bench, and speech-aware-annotations is restated as the annotation-only overlay profile covering TED-EL, HALAS and the SQuAD v1.1 dev reference. Profile membership of existing assets was unchanged.
